item.title: 'Will call Putin over pneumonic plague,' says Trump - what is happening in Russia?
item.description: A woman at the Irkutsk Anti-Plague Research Institute in Siberia reportedly died from pneumonia of unknown cause. While there are suggestions she may have contracted pneumonic plague, Russian authorities have not confirmed this diagnosis. The World Health Organisation assesses the risk of spreading beyond Russia as very low and is in contact with Russian officials. US President Donald Trump plans to discuss the case with Russian President Vladimir Putin soon.

item.title: Streamer Alleges Racial Profiling: Beard plans legal action; police deny claims
item.description: BenDaDonnn has broken his silence after being arrested in College Station and charged with evading arrest or detention. He says he was racially profiled and wrongfully detained and plans legal action. Police say he refused commands and tried to get away. His bond was $7,000, while his security guard Kenny Carter’s bond was $4,000.
item.dc:creator: Sumit Roy

item.title: Ludwig Shares MrBeast Request: streamer says YouTuber sought honest video feedback; jokes off paid promo
item.description: Ludwig Ahgren revealed that MrBeast contacted him after several months without speaking, sending a link to his latest video and asking for his thoughts. Ludwig said he agreed to watch it and promised to share his “unadulterated thoughts.” He also joked about whether he should get paid for the promotion. Separately, Ludwig struggled with the difficult Geometry Dash level “GRIEF” during a recent stream.
item.dc:creator: Global Sports Desk

item.title: 'Against all odds': Tennessee death row inmate Christa Pike awake after failed execution
item.description: Christa Pike, a death row inmate in Tennessee, is recovering at a hospital following a failed execution attempt. Her lawyers reported that she is awake and speaking after being unconscious for several days. Doctors say the extent of her recovery remains uncertain, and she might face a long rehabilitation process. Legal questions arise about whether Tennessee can execute her again after the failed lethal injection.
item.dc:creator: Yashasvi Vasistha

item.title: Lake Hartwell Shoreline Cleanup: Drought exposes long-hidden trash; volunteers pull record 36 tires
item.description: In a remarkable display of community spirit, volunteers have gathered over 8,300 pounds of litter from the shores of Lake Hartwell, driven by an ongoing drought that has unveiled hidden debris. Amid concerns regarding the Clemson Lower Diversion Dam Saddle Dike, the U.S. Army Corps of Engineers has enforced specific restrictions.
item.dc:creator: TOI Science Desk

item.title: Chang’e-6 soil reveals metallic iron in lunar samples; it may preserve clues to Moon’s lost magnetic field
item.description: Recent analysis of lunar soil samples returned by China's Chang’e-6 mission revealed a unique form of iron. This iron, γ-Fe, exhibits exceptional magnetic properties, which could provide insights into the Moon's ancient magnetic field. Researchers suggest that extreme impacts on the lunar surface caused the formation and preservation of this unusual iron. The findings could enhance our understanding of the Moon's geological history and its evolution over time.
item.dc:creator: TOI Science Desk

item.title: New dating rewrites history of Oklahoma meteor crater
item.description: Researchers from the University of Texas at Austin have traced the Ames meteor impact to approximately 370 million years ago, presenting a significant revision to the previously accepted estimate of 467 million years. This research connects the impact with the Frasnian-Famennian mass extinction event, employing zircon crystals to establish a more precise timeline, thus providing deeper insights into pivotal moments in Earth's geological history.
item.dc:creator: TOI Science Desk

item.title: Maryland manure-lagoon overflow kills nearly 11,000 fish across 25 species, officials say
item.description: A tragic incident has unfolded at Basin Run, where nearly 11,000 fish have succumbed to the consequences of a manure lagoon overflow from Kilby Farms. The Maryland Department of the Environment has traced the source of this discharge back to a series of ongoing pollution violations. Local residents, frustrated with the recurring environmental harm, are demanding accountability.

item.title: Scientists found a new magnetic mineral in Chang’e-6 Moon samples, preserved inside impact-glass particles
item.description: A groundbreaking discovery by researchers has unveiled a new magnetic mineral, γ-Fe, found in lunar samples from the Chang'e-6 mission. This remarkable find sheds light on the ancient magnetic environment of the Moon, now long lost. Detailed analysis of tiny iron particles within lunar impact glasses reveals that γ-Fe can maintain stable magnetic signals, potentially serving as a record of the Moon's magnetic history.

item.title: California schoolgirl's sewing project grows into nonprofit with 5,000+ care bags for women
item.description: Khloe Thompson, a California teenager, started making care bags for women in need after seeing homelessness. She founded the nonprofit Khloe Kares, which has distributed over 5,000 handmade bags containing personal-care items. The organization collaborates with local businesses and community groups to expand its outreach efforts. Thompson's initiatives have also included supporting children in Ghana and youth workshops on various topics. She received the George H.W.

item.title: Miami Beach’s historic Savoy Hotel could face demolition for a 38-story tower
item.description: Plans have been submitted to demolish much of the historic Savoy Hotel to construct a new 38-story tower. This project will utilize Florida's Live Local Act to overcome local zoning regulations and historic preservation concerns. The developer aims to retain a small section of the Savoy's facade and lobby in a nod to history. Local officials and preservationists have expressed strong opposition due to potential loss of cultural heritage.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: EPA removed more than 52,000 tons of PCB-contaminated soil from a New Jersey Superfund site
item.description: Cleanup efforts at the Unimatic Manufacturing Corporation Superfund Site in Fairfield, New Jersey have been completed. The US Environmental Protection Agency removed over 52,000 tons of contaminated soil and sediment from the site. As part of the process, the former manufacturing building was demolished to eliminate potential hazards. The areas were restored with clean material, and trees and shrubs were planted for ecological recovery.

item.title: Lithuania ready to cover cost if US establishes military base
item.description: Lithuanian Prime Minister Mindaugas Sinkevicius has declared his willingness to finance the establishment of a permanent US military base in Lithuania. Since 2019, Lithuania has been hosting a rotating US battalion and is eager for a long-term military presence. Concurrently, the Lithuanian parliament is considering lifting constitutional prohibitions on nuclear weapons, a move that has drawn sharp criticism from Russia, citing heightened regional tensions.
